ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, officers and UBOs against: (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) Global Affairs Canada's Canadian Sanctions Framework and regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17) and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2017, c 21); (iii) the OSFI sanctions list and FINTRAC suspicious-transaction indicators; and (iv) as a commercial overlay for USD payment rails via Shopify Payments and Stripe, the OFAC SDN list and US Commerce Department Entity List. PEP status is determined via automated adverse-media screening followed by enhanced due diligence; continuous monitoring applies for the life of the relationship with refresh at least every 24 months or upon any trigger event, consistent with FINTRAC guidance on client due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — official portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca — online name reservation service ('demande de réservation de nom') under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, arts 15-16.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), arts 14-28.1: every legal person established in Quebec must bear a distinctly French corporate name or a name with a French form; the REQ performs a grammatical and lexical analysis of the proposed name; transliteration into Latin script (e.g., unaccented pinyin) is generally rejected; a name composed of a registered trademark or an internationally known name may be admitted; a numerical designation (e.g., 1234-5678 Québec Inc.) is a compliant fallback; any English trade name requires a registered French version of the enterprise name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms evoking state authority or royalty: 'Canada', 'Québec', 'Provincial', 'Royal', 'Gouvernement' (require ministerial or Crown consent)
Financial and trust tokens: 'Banque', 'Trust', 'Fiducie', 'Capital', 'Prêt', 'Finance', 'Assurances' (require prior authorization or licensing by the Autorité des marchés financiers)
Reserved professional titles: 'Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Comptable', 'Ingénieur', 'Architecte', 'Médecin' (require proof of membership in the relevant professional order)
Educational-establishment terms: 'Université', 'Collège', 'Académie', 'Polytechnique' (require approval of the Ministère de l'Éducation)
Misleading scope descriptors: 'International', 'Global', 'Worldwide', 'Centre' without demonstrable operations (P-44.1, arts 15-16; QBCA, s 21.2)
Obscene, scandalous or public-order offences (P-44.1, art 16)
Confusingly similar or homophonic tokens already present in the REQ register, including identical distinctives with nominally different suffixes or diacritics

Anglicisms and French-language purity violations actionable by the Office québécois de la langue française (e.g., 'Keyboard Caps' as the only name form without a French dominant version such as 'Touches de clavier')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ refusal, the applicant: (1) receives written reasons; (2) may file a written application for review with the Registraire within 60 days of the refusal notice (P-44.1, art 17); (3) may contest an adverse review decision before the Court of Québec (Civil Division, district of Québec or Montréal) within 30 days of notification; and (4) may in parallel file a fresh reservation with a new distinctive coined element, which is the faster market practice. A reservation cannot be formally extended; if the 90-day window lapses, a new request and fee are required, subject to continued availability of the name. Federal CBCA incorporations instead undergo NUANS-based name clearance with a distinct conflict-analysis procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for the pre-operational phase only: a virtual or business-centre address in Quebec can serve as the registered office (siège social) for service of process and REQ registration purposes, but it cannot be the sole establishment once manufacturing commences. For ISIC 3240 / NAICS 334118 double-shot PBT injection molding, the REQ, Revenu Québec and municipal authorities will expect a real operational premise with machinery, raw-material storage and inventory; maintaining only a virtual address while operating a factory elsewhere creates false-declaration risk under P-44.1 and fiscal substance audit exposure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 60% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 operating months, rising to 90%+ within 36 months. Drivers: (i) REQ verification visits to confirm the physical establishment declared at registration; (ii) municipal fire-safety and Régie du bâtiment du Québec inspections because injection molding machines involve 200-280°C barrels, compressed-air systems and polymer-fume hazards; (iii) Revenu Québec GST/QST input-tax-credit audits triggered by heavy capital expenditure on molds and injection equipment; and (iv) Shopify Payments and Stripe merchant underwriting that requires documentary and physical-address verification for manufacturing merchants.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA) — ss. 7 (incorporation), 8 (contents of articles), 9 (name restrictions), 64-65 (first board organization), 84-87 (registered office), 127-133 (officers), 162-169 (bylaws); supplementary federal regime under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 not applied as registration is solely in Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registraire des entreprises, 500 boulevard Roland-LeGendre, Québec, Québec G2K 0N3; electronic filing via clicSÉAQ-Entreprises portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) submitted to the Registraire des entreprises under section 7 QBCA; the certificate of incorporation is conclusive evidence of corporate existence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under QBCA; incorporators may create corporations with nil authorized capital and a nominal paid-up amount. Share consideration is fixed by directors' resolution; no escrow account rule applies to ordinary non-public incorporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The registered office is fixed at 123 Promenade du Vieux-Montréal, Québec, Province of Québec and the directors instruct the Corporate Secretary to file the attestation of registered office and directors with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. 3. The following officers are appointed: [CEO], [CFO] and [Corporate Secretary], with full authority to open bank accounts and execute trade documents. 4. All preliminary acts connected to incorporation are ratified. Carried unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online clicSÉAQ-Entreprises; licensed NUANS report suppliers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS database search covering federal and Québec corporate records to confirm the proposed name is distinctive and does not infringe existing trademarks or corporation names. Include a legal element (Inc. or Corp.) and a descriptive or distinctive component. Retain the original NUANS report and, where a name is restricted or marks exist, file consent or alternative name clearance before submission of articles.
required_dossiers: Original NUANS name search report
Name reservation request form (if applicable)
Letter of consent from prior nameholder (where required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name conflicts with an existing registration, the incorporators may amend the distinctive element and resubmit the search, or provide a written consent from the registered holder. A name refusal by REQ may be administratively reconsidered within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Submit Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — clicSÉAQ-Entreprises electronic filing window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles under QBCA stating the corporate name, share structure (class rights, number and par value), transfer restrictions for a close corporation, and the number and category of directors. The incorporator(s) execute the articles digitally. Submit the filing online, pay the statutory application fee, and receive the certificate of incorporation electronically followed by the REQ registration file.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of incorporation (REQ electronic form)
NUANS name report in original
Statement of residence and consent to act of each director
Share capital structure and class rights schedule
Incorporators' mandate or proxy, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a non-compliance query, correct the stated omission in the articles and resubmit within 30 days without losing priority; if registration is refused, incorporators may file modified articles for a nominal fee or seek judicial rectification in accordance with section 14 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Attest Registered Office and Initial Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — attestation filing module.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within six months of incorporation, submit the attestation of registered office and directors to REQ identifying the exact municipal address of the registered office in Québec and the names and residential addresses of the directors. The initial directors execute consent to act forms. The attestation updates the public register and completes the standing record of the enterprise.
required_dossiers: Attestation of registered office and directors (REQ form)
First board resolution adopting the registered office
Directors' consents and residence particulars
Certificate of incorporation and NEQ slip
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation is not filed in the statutory six-month window, REQ may warn the corporation and proceed to dissolution. The cure is to file the attestation immediately with the applicable late fee and, if dissolution has commenced, petition for reinstatement under section 98 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Quebec Business Number and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — Entreprises service window and online customer space.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After REQ incorporation, the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) is automatically assigned. Register with Revenu Québec for Québec Sales Tax (TVQ/QST), and where employees exist, for QPP, QPIP, and other withholding source deductions. Confirm the establishment address for municipal tax and business purposes, and activate the enterprise online file.
required_dossiers: REQ registration certificate and NEQ confirmation
Business establishment address verification
Directors' and senior officers' identification and social insurance numbers
Bank account details for tax refunds and remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec queries the file for a mismatch of address or officer data, submit corrected information using the online customer space. Administrative review of QST registration or withholding changes is available through the Bureau de révision administrative within 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Federal Business Number and CRA Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the REQ corporate data to open a federal Business Number (BN). Register for GST/HST, payroll deductions (TPX) if employees are hired, and corporate income tax account RC169. Where the registrant uses Shopify Payments or Stripe, the BN and corporate registry linkage expedites merchant onboarding; the CRA confirmation letter acts as the non-financial compliance reference.
required_dossiers: REQ corporate registration data and NEQ
CRA RC169 Business Number registration worksheet
Directors' details for identity verification
Primary business activity code: NAICS 334118 (computer peripheral manufacturing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA account opening is rejected or PIN verification fails, the corporation may call the CRA Business Number call-in service to restore the account immediately. Errors in fiscal period or business activity are curable via the CRA online application or Form RC143.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt By-Law No. 1 and Complete Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the Corporation; corporate records maintained at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board convenes after incorporation and adopts By-Law No. 1 covering directors, officers, share issuance and transfer restrictions, borrowing powers, indemnification, and meeting procedures. Issue the subscribed share certificates, maintain the shareholders' register and directors register, and deposit into the statutory minute book all board resolutions, contracts, and banking mandates.
required_dossiers: By-Law No. 1 text
Share subscription agreement and certificates
Minute book, registers of directors and shareholders
Officer consents and banking resolution/account mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural omissions in the minute book or bylaw ratification may be cured by a validating board resolution without reincorporation. If a director exceeded stated authority, an unanimous shareholder agreement or subsequent board indemnification may ratify the act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction de l'enregistrement et de la conformité; and the municipal permitting office where the injection-molding unit is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'autorisation / Attestation de conformité under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) and the Déclaration de conformité réglementaire applicable to plastics processing; municipal industrial and business licence for the manufacturing premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — Declaration of conformity registration under the Règlement sur la déclaration de conformité (Q-2, r. 9.11) for thermoplastic injection molding; no full environmental impact assessment (Category I full authorization) is required where installed resin capacity, VOC emissions, and hazardous waste generation remain below regulated thresholds. If emissions exceed prescribed quantities, a full authorization impact analysis becomes mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Québec Clean Air Regulation (Q-2, r. 4.1) for stack and fugitive VOC and particulate limits; wastewater discharge into municipal sewers must comply with the applicable municipal sewer by-law and the Environment Quality Act (pH, BOD/COD, suspended solids); PBT/ABS scrap and dust must be directed to waste valorization streams; solvents, mold-release agents, and spent cleaning materials are managed as hazardous wastes under the Règlement sur les matières dangereuses (Q-2, r. 32), with generation manifests at threshold quantities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local fire safety authority under the Québec Building Code and Loi sur la sécurité incendie (CQLR c S-3.4); municipal structural and occupancy permits for machine loads; workplace health and safety registration with CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) including injection-molding press guarding, noise exposure controls, and emergency evacuation signage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online and My Business Account portals, for the federal Business Number and GST/HST administration; Revenu Québec, including the clicSÉQUR-Entreprises portal, for Québec Sales Tax (QST), Québec employer and source-deduction accounts, and related Québec tax registrations. Commercial importers and exporters also interact with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the CARM system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated federal or Québec corporation generally obtains a nine-digit CRA Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online, incorporation-related registration, telephone registration, or an authorized representative. The corporation then opens the applicable CRA program accounts, including RT for GST/HST, RM for import-export, RP for payroll, and RC for corporate income tax where required by CRA procedures. A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada, importing commercial goods, or otherwise required to register must apply for a BN and the relevant program accounts through CRA procedures; it should maintain a Canadian service address or authorized representative where required and provide incorporation documents, legal name, jurisdiction, directors, ownership information, business activities, effective dates, and authorized-contact details. A corporation carrying on business in Québec must register for a Québec identification number and applicable QST account with Revenu Québec. A GST/HST registrant making taxable supplies in Québec generally administers GST federally and QST separately with Revenu Québec. Commercial importers must obtain or activate an RM import-export account in CARM and satisfy CBSA importer-account requirements. Registration does not itself establish corporate income-tax residence; residence and permanent-establishment analysis remain separate questions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian corporation is ordinarily a separate taxpayer and has no United States-style check-the-box election. It may elect specific statutory regimes where legally eligible, including Canadian-controlled private corporation treatment based on ownership and control facts, associated-corporation rules, the small-business deduction regime, and certain status elections under the Income Tax Act. A corporation may also use permitted amalgamation, wind-up, rollover, or reorganization provisions, subject to statutory conditions. Partnerships and certain trusts may be fiscally transparent, but a corporation cannot generally elect to be treated as a partnership or pass-through entity for Canadian income-tax purposes. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules can deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences for specified mismatch arrangements; they do not create a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) administered by the CRA, combined in Québec with the Québec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec. GST applies at 5.0%; the Québec QST rate is generally 9.975%, producing a combined ordinary rate of 14.975% on supplies subject to both taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies, calculated under the applicable small-supplier rules, is the principal GST/HST registration threshold for most businesses. The threshold generally considers worldwide taxable supplies of the supplier and associated persons, subject to statutory exclusions and special rules. A person may register voluntarily below the threshold. Québec generally applies a CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST purposes, with separate rules for suppliers, specified Québec suppliers, non-resident suppliers, and taxable supplies made in Québec. Registration can also be required without relying solely on the threshold where the business is carrying on business in Canada or Québec, importing taxable commercial goods, or falls within a special registration regime. A non-resident e-commerce supplier should separately test ordinary GST/QST registration, the simplified GST/HST regime, and Québec specified-supplier rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not generally impose a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance or continuous transaction-control mandate for ordinary private-sector sales. Invoices and electronic records must contain information sufficient to support GST/HST and QST collection, input-tax-credit or input-tax-refund claims, tax calculation, and audit verification; required records must be retained for the statutory period, generally six years from the end of the relevant year unless a longer period or authorization applies. Electronic invoicing is generally permitted if records remain reliable, readable, accessible, and reproducible. CRA electronic filing and payment requirements apply to specified registrants and circumstances, and Revenu Québec has separate electronic-filing obligations for designated taxpayers. Commercial import declarations and accounting are filed through CBSA CARM; customs data may be transmitted electronically, but ordinary keyboard-keycap sales are not subject to a general fiscal e-invoice pre-clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For GST purposes, qualifying exports of tangible goods are generally zero-rated where the goods are supplied for export and the statutory delivery, possession, shipping, or export conditions are satisfied. Evidence should demonstrate that the goods left Canada or were delivered to a non-resident in circumstances prescribed by the Excise Tax Act and its regulations. Goods shipped directly from Canada to a foreign customer normally require commercial shipping and customs evidence linking the sale, goods, purchaser, carrier, and export. Goods supplied to a non-resident but delivered in Canada do not automatically qualify. Services may be zero-rated where they are supplied to a non-resident and satisfy the specific exported-service rules; many services connected with real property, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or services performed in Canada are excluded. QST treatment must be tested separately; qualifying exports of movable property from Québec and qualifying services supplied outside Québec may be zero-rated or outside the QST base under Québec legislation, but the precise statutory conditions and documentary evidence differ. Input tax credits and input-tax refunds require valid tax documentation, proof of commercial use, and reconciliation to returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the Canadian supplier, foreign purchaser, goods description, quantity, value, currency, terms of sale, and destination
CBSA export declaration or applicable electronic export-reporting record, including the applicable reporting exemption analysis where no declaration is required
Canada Customs Invoice or equivalent commercial documentation where required by CBSA or the carrier
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, postal record, or other carrier document showing shipment from Canada to the foreign destination
Packing list and shipment records linking the exported goods to the customer invoice and production or inventory records
Proof of delivery or foreign import/customs record where available
Purchase order, sales contract, payment record, and customer correspondence establishing the foreign transaction
Foreign purchaser and destination evidence, including non-resident status where relevant

For zero-rated services, contract, statement of work, deliverables, location-of-performance evidence, customer residency evidence, and records proving satisfaction of the applicable exported-service rule
GST/QST return workpapers reconciling zero-rated revenue, export documentation, collected tax, input tax credits, and input tax refunds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated to Canada within 180 days or another fixed period. Export proceeds may remain abroad, subject to ordinary income-tax, transfer-pricing, foreign-exchange reporting, anti-money-laundering, customs, and corporate-record requirements. During an audit, CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating where export, non-resident, destination, delivery, or service-location evidence is insufficient and assess GST or QST, applicable interest, and consequential reassessments of net tax, input tax credits, or refunds. False statements or omissions may attract statutory penalties, including gross-negligence penalties where the legal test is met; deliberate fraud or tax evasion may result in prosecution and fines or imprisonment. Improperly obtained refunds can be reassessed and recovered with interest. Customs non-compliance may trigger CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalty System sanctions, reassessment of duties and taxes, seizure or detention in appropriate cases, and other enforcement measures. Documentary retention, transaction-level reconciliation, and prompt correction of unsupported zero-rated claims are essential.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); regulatory coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada does not maintain a dedicated exchange-control administration or foreign-exchange licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Capital controls are not imposed; non-residents may freely invest, operate, repatriate capital, and remit dividends, interest, royalties, and loan repayments without prior regulatory approval, subject only to corporate solvency tests, tax withholding rules, and FINTRAC reporting obligations. There are no currency licensing, approval, or quota requirements applicable to a Quebec business corporation in the keycap manufacturing sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters are free to retain foreign-currency earnings in domestic or offshore bank accounts and may convert to Canadian dollars at their commercial discretion. For statistical balance-of-payments purposes, exporters must report annual export values to Statistics Canada through the Canadian International Merchandise Trade returns; however, this is purely informational and does not impose surrender or conversion obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary collection rail, Low as the primary treasury hub. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise Business, Mercury, or Payoneer can provide multi-currency account numbers and low-cost card operations, but they are not chartered Canadian banks, do not offer CDIC deposit insurance, and cannot provide standard Canadian clearing codes for direct deposits or pre-authorized debits. Legally, an EMI directing services into Canada is required to register as a money service business with FINTRAC; a Quebec corporate client must still independently comply with FINTRAC wire-reporting thresholds and cannot rely on the offshore EMI to perform its Canadian AML obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted under FINTRAC's risk-based approach and is supported by all tier-1 Canadian banks. Canadian-resident directors do not need to attend a branch in person; video-call identity verification, electronic signatures, scanned government credentials, and registraire des entreprises attestations are acceptable. For accounts involving non-resident beneficial owners, capital escrow purposes, or high transaction velocity, banks may require at least one Canadian-resident director or an authorized financial intermediary to complete an in-person interview at the account-opening branch. Foreign directors can satisfy KYC remotely using notarized passports, apostilled corporate resolutions, bank references, and sworn source-of-wealth declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership, especially through an offshore holding company, blocks account opening at the underwriting stage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charter, Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation, up-to-date beneficial ownership register, passports and proof of address for each direct and indirect owner, source-of-funds bank statements, notarized board resolution appointing a Canadian-resident authorized signatory, and a corporate organizational chart showing full ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial foreign capital injection arrives before the company has a revenue trail, supplier invoices, or historical financial statements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution agreement, share issuance minutes, investor resolution, six-month business plan, cash-flow forecast, manufacturing supply quotations, independent valuation of injected assets, sworn declaration of source of wealth, and an explanatory memorandum linking funds to the keycap injection moulding business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-value card settlements from Shopify and Stripe appear inconsistent with a physical manufacturing entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce merchant agreements, platform KYC verifications, settled payout reports, product catalog URLs, unit pricing and bill of materials, refund and chargeback histories, inventory reconciliation, injection-moulding equipment purchase invoices, and a commercial lease for the production facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border SWIFT MT103 disbursements to Asian tooling and PBT resin suppliers trigger trade-based money-laundering flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master supply agreement, purchase orders, commercial invoices with HTS/HS classification codes, bills of lading or airway bills, cargo insurance documents, CBSA customs entries, supplier bank identifier confirmations, letters of credit or documentary collection records, and a monthly payment schedule matching shipment milestones.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 using the purpose code for equity capital formation or investment. Beneficiary name and account number must exactly match the Canadian bank records; reference fields should include the corporate name, share certificate number, and a clear statement of 'equity injection for working capital'. For wires at or above CAD 10,000, the receiving Canadian bank will file an Incoming International Electronic Funds Transfer report with FINTRAC. To clear the funds without delay, provide the bank with a board resolution authorizing the issuance of shares, a complete shareholder register, source-of-wealth evidence, and a use-of-funds breakdown showing mould tooling, resin purchases, and operational expenditures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments should use SWIFT MT103 for disbursements below USD 50,000, with the appropriate goods-trade purpose code, beneficiary BIC, account number, and invoice references. For larger or recurring resin and tooling purchases, commercial documentary letters of credit (L/C at sight) are the preferred clearing rail through the Canadian issuing bank to the supplier's confirming bank. For North American and European suppliers, USD ACH and SEPA rails can be used when a correspondent account allows it; all other corridors must clear via SWIFT correspondent banking. The treasury function should pre-submit the monthly disbursement schedule and supporting commercial documents to minimize false-positive trade-based money-laundering alerts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards up to 12 months with a Schedule I Canadian bank
CAD/USD FX options and zero-cost collars
Cross-currency interest rate swaps fully documented under ISDA 2002
CAD/USD FX swaps for liquidity management
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for third-country non-convertible currencies; never required for CAD/USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registraire des entreprises annual declaration (Déclaration annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the company's incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the deadline triggers a default notice from REQ; continued failure for one or two years may result in administrative dissolution or strike-off of the corporate entity, plus fines of up to CAD 2,000 for directors or officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the sixth month after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalized at 5% of the balance of tax owing plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12%); evidence of wilful neglect may lead to higher fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada federal corporation income tax return (T2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the sixth month after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties are 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months); where a return is terminated, an additional penalty may be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) (submitted as part of the annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary deadline as the annual declaration; any change in significant control must be recorded within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the ISC register can lead to fines up to CAD 25,000 for directors or senior officers; continued omissions may lead to a certificate of default from REQ.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), no statutory audit is compulsory for a private business corporation provided all shareholders unanimously resolve to waive the auditors' appointment. An audit is mandatory for offering (public) corporations or if a shareholder or the court requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private corporations may prepare financial statements in accordance with Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); federal and provincial regulators accept ASPE for non-public enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep a complete and accurate Register of Individuals with Significant Control, record any change within 15 calendar days, and annually confirm the register's consistency as part of the REQ declaration. Know-your-client and economic-residency checks are applied for foreign shareholders.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute book (minutes of directors' and shareholders' meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 – USD 350 per year for a registered office and corporate agent in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 12,000 for a typical small Quebec private business corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general rate 15%; Quebec general rate 11.5%; combined headline 26.5%; reduced combined 12.2% on first C$500,000 qualifying active business income (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% SBD rate, as reduced from 2023).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% on first C$500,000 of active business income of a CCPC; Quebec SBD reduces provincial rate to 3.2% (2023) on first C$500,000; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credits (35% for CCPC up to C$3,000,000 qualifying expenditures); Quebec innovation tax credit (up to 30% refundable for eligible R&D salaries); accelerated capital cost allowance (Class 50/53, 100% for zero-emission technology vehicles/assets). Excluded for personal services business income (s. 125(7) ITA).
